title: The Instant After: が早いか, や否や, なり, そばから, とみるや, た拍子に
description: Six ways to say 'the moment …' — and what each one can't do (no requests, no speaker's own plans, accidents only …).

points.title: 〜が早いか: no sooner than
points.summary: Dictionary / た-form + が早いか = the instant A happened, B followed. Narrative only — no requests or intentions in B.
points.body:
- ベルが鳴る**が早いか**、生徒たちは教室を飛び出した.
- Written, a little dramatic. B is something that actually happened.
examples: ベルが{鳴|な}るが{早|はや}いか、{生徒|せいと}たちは{教室|きょうしつ}を{飛|と}び{出|だ}した。
No sooner had the bell rung than the students dashed out of the classroom.

points.title: 〜や否や: the moment
points.summary: Dictionary form + や否や (やいなや) = as soon as. Close to が早いか; also narrative only.
points.body:
- ドアが開く**や否や**、乗客が降りてきた.
- Don't confuse with か否か (whether or not).
examples: ドアが{開|ひら}くや{否|いな}や、{乗客|じょうきゃく}が{一斉|いっせい}に{降|お}りてきた。
The moment the doors opened, the passengers all poured out.

points.title: 〜なり: as soon as (and then, unexpectedly)
points.summary: Dictionary form + なり = as soon as A, the same person did B (often surprising). Third person; not for the speaker's own plans, requests or commands.
points.body:
- 彼は部屋に入る**なり**、窓を全部開けた.
- ~~家に着くなり電話してください~~ ✗
examples: {彼|かれ}は{部屋|へや}に{入|はい}るなり、{窓|まど}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{開|あ}けた。
As soon as he walked into the room, he opened all the windows.

points.title: 〜そばから: no sooner … than (again and again)
points.summary: Dictionary / た-form + そばから = right after A, B undoes it — a repeated, frustrating cycle.
points.body:
- 片付ける**そばから**、子供が散らかしていく.
- 習った**そばから**忘れてしまう.
examples: {習|なら}ったそばから{忘|わす}れてしまう。
I forget things as soon as I've learned them.

points.title: 〜とみるや: on seeing that, immediately
points.summary: Plain form + と見るや = judging that A (from what you see), one immediately did B.
points.body: - 形勢が不利だ**と見るや**、彼はすぐに作戦を変えた.
examples: {形勢|けいせい}が{不利|ふり}だと{見|み}るや、{彼|かれ}はすぐに{作戦|さくせん}を{変|か}えた。
The moment he saw things were going badly, he changed his tactics.

points.title: 〜た拍子に: in the instant (accidentally)
points.summary: た-form + 拍子に = in the sudden movement of A, something unintended happened.
points.body:
- 転んだ**拍子に**眼鏡を落とした.
- くしゃみをした**拍子に**腰を痛めた.
examples: {転|ころ}んだ{拍子|ひょうし}に、{眼鏡|めがね}を{落|お}としてしまった。
When I fell, my glasses went flying.

questions.prompt: ベルが{鳴|な}る（　）、{生徒|せいと}たちは{教室|きょうしつ}を{飛|と}び{出|だ}した。
notes: がてら = 'while also (doing)' — needs a noun like 散歩.
が最後 = 'once …, (there's no stopping it)' — for the start of something irreversible.
が限り isn't a pattern (限り follows without が).
questions.translation: No sooner had the bell rung than the students dashed out of the classroom.

questions.prompt: {彼|かれ}は{家|いえ}に{帰|かえ}る（　）、ベッドに{倒|たお}れ{込|こ}んだ。
notes: 帰りがてら = 'on the way home' — the noun form, and no instant sequence.
ものの = 'although'.
が最後 needs something that can't be stopped afterwards.
questions.translation: The second he got home, he collapsed onto the bed.

questions.prompt: {電車|でんしゃ}のドアが{開|ひら}く（　）、{乗客|じょうきゃく}が{一斉|いっせい}に{降|お}りてきた。
notes: やら = listing ('what with …').
か否か = 'whether or not'.
ものなら = 'if (one could)'.
questions.translation: The moment the train doors opened, the passengers all poured out.

questions.prompt: What does 「{彼女|かのじょ}は{私|わたし}の{顔|かお}を{見|み}るや{否|いな}や、{泣|な}き{出|だ}した。」 mean?
options: Whether or not she saw my face, she cried.
Before she saw my face, she was crying.
The moment she saw my face, she burst into tears.
Although she saw my face, she cried.
notes: That would be か否か.
や否や = right after, not before.
No concession here.

questions.prompt: {彼|かれ}は{部屋|へや}に{入|はい}る（　）、{窓|まど}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{開|あ}けた。
notes: なりに = 'in one's own way'.
なりの needs a noun after it.
なりとも = 'even a little'.
questions.translation: As soon as he walked into the room, he opened all the windows.

options: {家|いえ}に{着|つ}くなり、{電話|でんわ}してください。
{彼|かれ}は{電話|でんわ}を{切|き}るなり、{出|で}かけて{行|い}った。
{私|わたし}は{家|いえ}に{着|つ}くなり、すぐ{電話|でんわ}します。
{彼|かれ}は{電話|でんわ}を{切|き}るなりに、{出|で}かけて{行|い}った。
notes: なり can't be followed by a request.
なり isn't used for the speaker's own plans.
なりに = 'in one's own way'.
questions.translation: As soon as he hung up, he went out.

questions.prompt: {片付|かたづ}ける（　）、{子供|こども}が{散|ち}らかしていく。
notes: からして = 'judging from / to begin with'.
そばに = 'next to'.
ところから = 'from the fact that'.
questions.translation: As fast as I tidy up, the kids make a mess again.

questions.prompt: What does 「{習|なら}ったそばから{忘|わす}れてしまう。」 mean?
options: I learn things after I've forgotten them.
I forget things I learned next to someone.
I never forget what I've learned.
I forget things as soon as I've learned them.
questions.explanation: そばから = **right after, again and again**.
notes: The order is learn → forget.
そば here isn't 'beside'.
The opposite.

questions.prompt: {形勢|けいせい}が{不利|ふり}だと（　）、{彼|かれ}はすぐに{作戦|さくせん}を{変|か}えた。
notes: と見ても = 'even if one judges'.
と見るなら = 'if one judges' — but he already acted.
と見るから isn't a pattern.
questions.translation: The moment he saw things were going badly, he changed his tactics.

questions.prompt: {客|きゃく}が{来|き}たと（　）、{店員|てんいん}はさっと{笑顔|えがお}になった。
notes: 見えて doesn't take と + clause this way.
見せて = 'showing'.
見るに = 'looking at it (judging)' — not an instant reaction.
questions.translation: The moment the shop assistant saw a customer coming, she broke into a smile.

questions.prompt: {転|ころ}んだ（　）、{眼鏡|めがね}を{落|お}としてしまった。
notes: 拍手 = 'applause'.
様子 = 'appearance'.
調子に乗る = 'get carried away' — not this.
questions.translation: When I fell, I dropped my glasses.

questions.prompt: What does 「くしゃみをした{拍子|ひょうし}に、{腰|こし}を{痛|いた}めた。」 mean?
options: I hurt my back, then sneezed.
I hurt my back when I sneezed.
I sneezed because my back hurt.
I sneezed rhythmically and hurt my back.
notes: The order is sneeze → injury.
The sneeze caused it, not the other way round.
拍子 isn't rhythm here.
